approachQuestion.prompt:
Crew Split. A non-empty binary tree with n>=2 nodes represents a connected organization. Remove exactly one parent-child link, producing two connected components. Return the smallest possible absolute difference between their node counts. Labels do not affect the counts; return only the difference, not the chosen link.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: 1(2(4(-,-),5(-,-)),3(-,-)), n=5. Output: 1, by removing link 1–2 to make sizes 3 and 2. Example 2: Input: 8(-,9(-,10(-,11(-,-)))), n=4. Output: 0, by cutting 9–10. Example 3: Input: 6(7(-,-),-), n=2. Output: 0.

Constraints: 2 <= n <= 200000; n is accurately supplied. Labels are signed 32-bit integers, possibly repeated. The immutable tree has child pointers only, no parent pointers, cycles or shared nodes; shape is unrestricted. Evaluate possible cuts without modifying the tree.

options.text: Use postorder frames to return each subtree size. For each non-root node with subtree size s, consider the cut to its parent using component sizes s and n-s. Keep the least absolute difference.
options.feedback: Every removable link corresponds to exactly one non-root subtree. The remaining nodes form the other connected component, so n-s counts all of them.

options.text: For every parent-child link, run a fresh traversal of the child subtree to count s; compare s with n-s and keep the least difference.
options.feedback: This evaluates every legal cut correctly, but the size scans overlap. Computing sizes once from the children removes the repeated scans.

options.text: Compare only the root’s left and right subtree sizes and return their absolute difference.
options.feedback: Removing one link does not delete the root, and a best cut may be deeper. Example 2 has root child sizes 0 and 3, while the correct answer is 0.

options.text: Also treat s=n at the root as a candidate whose difference is zero, since all nodes stay together.
options.feedback: Exactly one link must be removed and both components must be non-empty. For 1(2(-,-),3(-,-)) every legal cut gives sizes 1 and 2 and answer 1, not the invented zero.

feedback.reason: A removed edge separates one subtree from its complement; the outside component must use n minus subtree size.
details: Use fixed-size postorder frames to combine size 1+leftSize+rightSize, with missing size zero. For every completed non-root frame update the minimum with abs(n-2*size). Do not treat the root as a cut. Pass only size upward and release the child frame; retain no table of all sizes.

Removing a non-root subtree of size s leaves components s and n-s, whose difference is abs(n-2s). The root has no parent edge and is not a legal cut. Fixed-size returned sizes avoid a table for all subtrees.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the revealed postorder cut method let n be the supplied node count and h the height in nodes. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Count frames, fixed-size partial counts, and global minimum. Exclude the input and scalar output. Counts and n-2*s fit machine integers; no tree links are changed and no subtree is rescanned.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: Each node contributes one size combine and at most one cut candidate.
details: Each node combines sizes once and each non-root node contributes one constant-time cut candidate. Only O(h) active ancestor frames and fixed-size partial results remain live; a chain attains h frames.

Removing a link to child v disconnects exactly v’s subtree of size s from the other n-s nodes. Every link has one such child, so considering all non-root nodes enumerates all and only legal cuts; minimizing their differences is sufficient.

“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Each node combines sizes once and each non-root node contributes one constant-time cut candidate. Only O(h) active ancestor frames and fixed-size partial results remain live; a chain attains h frames.
“O(n²) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Completed subtrees are not scanned again; nesting the control flow does not itself multiply the node visits.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The live explicit stack is auxiliary memory and can grow with tree height.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is a looser upper bound since h <= n; the height-sensitive bound is tighter and no full node table is retained.
